intervention: Steam spinach or broccoli rather than the tested boiling preparation

moa.description: Avoiding immersion may reduce leaching; thermal degradation is another possible source of loss.
moa.evidenceQualification: Contributions were not isolated. No controlled short mechanism identity assigned.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: Higher total-folate retention under the tested vegetable steaming conditions than boiling.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Preservation of an admitted dietary precursor for the 5-MTHF donor; no measured human remethylation response.

evidenceSource.exposure: 25-g raw-weight portions; typical spinach steaming/boiling 3/3.5 minutes, broccoli 10/10 minutes
evidenceSource.design: Three independent occasions with duplicate food portions; food-composition assay, not human feeding

limitations.text: Total folate retention is not absorption, 5-MTHF concentration or remethylation flux.
Tested potato boiling and beef grilling did not significantly reduce folate.
Folate preservation does not establish superiority for other objectives such as oxalate removal.

candidateOrigin: BRAIN food-page preparation screen followed by original-paper retrieval
